objective: Attach disjoint selected causal-record pages from a live scheduler-owned source request to a borrower without gathering, serializing, loading, copying, or re-encoding selected K/V.

verdict.reason: The connector can retain scheduler blocks, but it cannot insert arbitrary retained block IDs into a new request's scheduler-owned req_to_blocks/table. The only external-load API returns a token count, after which KVCacheManager allocates fresh destination blocks. build_connector_meta is explicitly forbidden from modifying SchedulerOutput. Worker block tables only consume scheduler-provided block IDs. A PRA-only monkey patch could rewrite the worker attention table, but that leaves scheduler ownership/accounting unaware and is not a supported zero-copy implementation.

pinned_api_evidence.finding: bind_gpu_block_pool exposes BlockPool, which is sufficient to touch/free source pages but does not expose per-request req_to_blocks.
get_num_new_matched_tokens returns only a prefix token count and requires the largest available prompt prefix; it cannot return existing physical block IDs or sparse logical positions.
update_state_after_alloc receives blocks only after CacheManager has allocated them; it cannot replace allocation with aliases.
build_connector_meta explicitly MUST NOT modify SchedulerOutput.
External matched tokens are routed to allocate_external_computed_blocks after local hits are touched.
allocate_external_computed_blocks calls block_pool.get_new_blocks and appends fresh destination blocks; no alias parameter exists.
touch/free_blocks provide correct shared-page reference counting and eviction protection once blocks are attached or explicitly pinned.
NewRequestData is constructed from KVCacheManager-owned request block IDs before connector metadata is built.
The legacy worker BlockTable can append arbitrary IDs internally, but the connector is not given a supported method to alter its rows.
The worker populates persistent request block rows from scheduler-provided new_block_ids; connector metadata does not participate in that row construction.

negative_api_search.note: The sole 'adopt' match is an unrelated scheduler comment about a cache decision, not a connector API.

current_real_qwen_control.interpretation: The current path proves same-subset correctness and resident reuse after first load, but it is not zero-copy: each selected resource is gathered to a derived payload and copied back to GPU once.

why_apc_is_not_a_substitute: Prefix-cache lookup is a token-prefix operation, while PRA selection is an ordered set of disjoint causal pages.
Selected pages do not form the original parent-hash chain after omitted pages are removed.
The borrower sends only the query suffix, so ordinary APC cannot infer or attach the selected source page IDs.
Original RoPE extent differs from the compact selected-token count and needs an explicit position base.

required_upstream_patch.new_scheduler_contract: A KV connector may return per-KV-group existing block IDs plus logical selected length, original position extent, immutable source generation, and ownership token for a new request.
validation: Reject block IDs outside the scheduler BlockPool.
Reject duplicates unless the engine explicitly supports repeated logical pages.
Require full-block alignment for the first implementation.
Validate group count, block size, model/cache identity, source generation, and original position extent.
Reject aliases whose owner pin is absent or stale.
required_upstream_patch.allocation: KVCacheManager must atomically touch the supplied existing blocks, install them into every manager's req_to_blocks, mark only those selected tokens computed, and allocate fresh blocks solely for the query/output suffix.
required_upstream_patch.scheduler_output: NewRequestData/CachedRequestData must carry the aliased block IDs as the request's authoritative block table; no worker-side rewrite is allowed.
required_upstream_patch.positions: Scheduler/model-runner metadata must carry selected logical length separately from original source_position_base so attention reads selected pages while new query positions retain their original extent.
required_upstream_patch.lifecycle: The resource owner holds one BlockPool reference; each borrower obtains another atomically. Cancellation/termination releases only the borrower reference. Eviction/offload requires zero borrowers, invalidates the generation, and then releases the owner reference.
required_upstream_patch.telemetry: Report alias_block_count, owner_refcount, borrower_refcount, selected_text_reencoded_tokens=0, selection_materialization_kv_copy_bytes=0, attachment_h2d_bytes=0, attachment_d2d_bytes=0, and newly_evaluated_suffix_tokens separately.

qualification_plan_after_patch: Unit-test disjoint multi-page aliases, duplicate/out-of-range/stale rejection, atomic rollback on partial failure, and refcount balance.
Run the frozen Qwen Task02 subset reference: direct alias and same-subset fresh reference must emit identical temperature-zero token IDs.
Require zero gather/serialization files, zero selected K/V copy bytes, zero H2D/D2D attachment bytes, and unchanged physical page IDs from source to borrowers.

Repeat with two concurrent borrowers, cancellation of one, normal termination of the other, stale-generation rejection, owner eviction, and exact offload/restore where restore is explicitly measured as a load rather than zero-copy.
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not call BlockTable.add_row/append_row from connector code without scheduler ownership updates.
Do not mutate SchedulerOutput inside build_connector_meta.
Do not claim the current detached-tail or worker attention-table monkey patch as scheduler-owned zero-copy.
Do not label a resident second-borrower hit as end-to-end zero-copy when first materialization copied 804651008 bytes.
